# Task handoff

## Identity

Task ID:  
Requirement IDs:  
Implementing commit/branch:  
Status: NOT_STARTED / IN_PROGRESS / IN_REVIEW / DONE / BLOCKED / approved NOT_APPLICABLE

## Intended and delivered outcome

Describe the one user-visible or technical outcome. State what was not changed. Include whether the repository is greenfield or existing implementation.

## Files and contracts

List exact changed files; explain each migration, generated API/client change, permission/state rule and module boundary touched. Confirm no unrelated changes.

## Dependency evidence

List added/updated exact versions, engine/peer intersection, lockfile hash, licenses/advisories and native/browser/provider smoke results. Write “no dependency changes” when true. Link the compatibility evidence.

## Decisions

List applicable D01–D12 approvals. Pending professional policy is a blocker for affected behavior; it is not replaced by a developer assumption.

## Executed verification

| Command / test | Tested artifact and fixture | Actual result / exit status | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pending | Pending | NOT RUN | — |

State intended test counts and actual discovered counts. Do not copy planned commands into this table as passing tests. Distinguish unit/mocked evidence from real-service/provider evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

Record AC1/AC2/AC3 and their corresponding assertions. Include denied/failure/race cases and remaining limitations.

## Recovery and authorization

Explain failure handling and migration/data-repair bounds. Record separate merge/deployment authorization only if actually received; this handoff does not grant it.

## Review and next task

Reviewer:  
Review result:  
Open blockers:  
Next eligible task by dependency order:  
Stop after this task; do not implement the next one without assignment.
